headline: US soybean shipments to China rebound in September after a year of zero imports
hook: China's soy demand lifts US exports
summary: China imported US soybeans in September, reversing a complete halt the previous year. The rebound reflects easing of trade tensions and strong domestic demand for feed and oil. US soybean exporters benefit from the renewed market, while global soybean prices have slipped. Indian edible‑oil producers and feed manufacturers may see lower input costs, affecting related stocks.
whats_next: USDA soybean export report due Oct 2026
why_it_matters: Cheaper soybean oil for Indian consumers
winners_losers: US exporters gain / Indian importers gain
